title: I Just Bought $30,000 of a NEW stock
creator: Joseph Carlson After Hours
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; note: captions garble the membership name as 'Qualtra/Qualum/Qualra'
summary: Joseph Carlson welcomes Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia, driven by President Trump's personal intervention, but with reservations: he would have preferred Nvidia's board to reinstate Jensen autonomously, says a president intervening in a public company's board sets a bad precedent, and warns investigations of Jensen will keep coming - though he stresses Jensen did real wrong and also should not be permanently barred. He held Nvidia as his number-one buy through the drop and keeps it a BUY. The main event is his new position: he bought $30,000 of Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) today at about $360 (he had planned $315-330 before the Jensen news jumped it $30) and will add another $30,000 in three $10,000 tranches on each $20 drop, building a $60,000 position with a $450 fair value. His thesis: TSM holds about 70% of high-end chip manufacturing, is effectively irreplaceable, trades at the low end of its historical valuation (about 21x trailing P/E versus a 24x median), grows earnings 35-36% and is building 19 new fabs. He ranks the semiconductor moat ladder as ASML at the top, then TSM, then Nvidia and AMD, with memory, neoclouds and energy the most commoditized. He considered Nvidia, AMD, Micron, SanDisk, Nebius and CoreWeave but picked TSM, and he discounts a China invasion of Taiwan as very unlikely. Calls: TSM BUY (executed, first actual buy), NVDA BUY reiterated.

calls.thesis: BUY reiterated - was BUY 16 Nov ('looking at adding it'), now executed: bought $30,000 at ~$360 today and plans another $30,000 in three $10,000 tranches on each $20 drop, for a $60,000 position. Fair value ~$450: it only needs to meet current analyst estimates to get there. ~70% share of high-end chip manufacturing, irreplaceable, at the low end of its historical valuation (~21x trailing P/E vs ~24x median, vs 46x peak), earnings growing 35-36%, building 19 new fabs, free cash flow seen at ~$70B by 2028. The 26% sell-off from highs was non-fundamental (politics + Jensen's ouster), so it can trade back up for non-fundamental reasons too.
calls.base_case: Meets current guidance and grinds toward $450 on earnings growth alone; each $20 drop triggers another $10,000 tranche.
calls.bull_case: Guidance gets raised and the multiple expands back toward its 46x peak as enthusiasm returns to the whole semiconductor chain.
calls.bear_case: Guidance gets cut instead; China/Taiwan geopolitical risk - he discounts an invasion as very unlikely, but a full invasion would be a global event hitting every AI stock, not just TSM.

calls.thesis: BUY reiterated (was BUY 16 Nov) - NVDA has been his number-one buy for the past couple of weeks and he held it as a top buy as it dropped ~30%. Jensen's return removes the unpredictability investors were pricing in, so the stock trades back up immediately (up ~35% on the day). He is glad overall - Jensen is an incredible leader and likely learned his lesson - but unhappy the president personally intervened in a public company's board: he would have preferred the board to reinstate Jensen autonomously, and Trump stepping in does not mean Jensen did nothing wrong. Investigations will keep coming and Nvidia investors must be ready for that political theme.
calls.base_case: Jensen back + renewed enthusiasm across the semiconductor chain; NVDA trades back up with predictability restored.
calls.bull_case: Jensen is more motivated than ever and the whole AI ecosystem re-rates as money pours back in.
calls.bear_case: Ongoing investigations and political attacks on Jensen drag on; he stresses NVDA would have been fine even without Jensen, so the premium is about predictability, not survival.
